stageA.warmup: Notice and Wonder transport image types: walk/car/train/school bus; pair discussion
stageA.activity1: Students truthfully identify their own travel mode today, create an initially freely arranged class display; teacher does not enforce grouping at this point
stageA.activity2: Reorganize SAME actual responses into a clearer student-authored grouped visual, pictures, tally marks, category names; compare two representations
stageA.synthesis: Teacher facilitates comparison of displays and explaining that grouped labels make counts clearer
stageA.sourceCoolDown: Publisher Organize Data restricted; independently authored Edulytics real-observation regrouping/interpretation check, not copied
stageA.visualRights: Independent pictograms and CSS response chips only, no publisher images
stageA.authenticDataRule: Real anonymous classroom data supplied by learners/teacher only; no generated classmates or fabricated categories

stageB.sourceAlignment: Initial unorganized genuine class responses deliberately permitted, authentic dataset not simulated, student's second display reorganizes SAME observations, classroom discussion rubric preserved
stageB.sourceGuard: original source URL/body SHA, ordered official outcome codes and old learner prose exactly verified before replacing

stageC.teacherRubric: Real classroom survey, child-designed representation and gallery walk explanations require teacher not just numerical marking
stageC.originalSourceActivityLearning: Warm-up transport categories, original unorganized responses, grouped pictograph with same counts, visual comparison
stageC.authoredCoolDown: Real classroom input drives exact group counts, total participants, bus category, absolute car vs train comparison; missing data not silently mocked
stageC.privacy: No names accepted, only categories and no official mark/response database write by companion activity
stageC.independentVisuals: Emoji pictograms and grouped CSS symbols, no original publisher imagery

closure.note: Authoring complete; Stage D separate verification of compilation, student view, tests, acceptance and release policy.
